proof_spans.label: the author's own proof environment immediately following the lemma: given s, t in the Picard functor over T, seek a locally closed Z with the universal property; first reduce (fppf-locally) to the case where s and t come from invertible modules: over an fppf covering {T_i} the restrictions give locally closed Z_i with the universal property, Z_i and Z_j agree on the common base (same scheme-theoretic inverse image), giving a descent datum; the locally quasi-finite morphisms Z_i -> T_i descend to Z -> T by the More on Morphisms lemma, Z -> T is an immersion by the Descent lemma, and the fppf-sheaf property of the Picard functor gives s|_Z = t|_Z and the universal property; in the invertible-module case set L = V x W^-1 and the desired Z is exactly the locus where L_{X_{T'}} is a pullback from T', which exists by the More on Morphisms of Spaces diagonal-Picard lemma (source lines 3282-3320)

core_obligations: Reduction to invertible modules (proof lines 3289-3307): over an fppf covering the restrictions s|_{T_i}, t|_{T_i} come from Pic(X_{T_i}); the resulting Z_i agree on overlaps, giving a descent datum; locally quasi-finite morphisms descend (More on Morphisms lemma), immersions descend (Descent lemma), and the fppf-sheaf property gives s|_Z = t|_Z plus the universal property.

Invertible-module case (proof lines 3310-3320): with L = V x W^-1, the desired Z is the locus where L_{X_{T'}} is a pullback of an invertible sheaf on T' (characterized by the quot exactness lemma), and Z exists by the More on Morphisms of Spaces diagonal-Picard lemma.
proof_roadmap: Set up the universal property for the equalizer of s and t (proof lines 3283-3286).
Descend the fppf-local solutions Z_i to a globally defined immersion Z -> T (proof lines 3289-3307).
Finish the invertible-module case by the diagonal-Picard lemma (proof lines 3310-3320).
